keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Lai). The infobox gives 'Established: ?', 'Conquered by Qi: 567 BC'; 'Lai was a large state'. No area on the page; Qi's pre-567 shape in Cliopatria (ea-01-b) is the control. The three discs (Changle-Weifang 45 km, Longkou 70 km, Yantai 70 km) are a stand-in for eastern Shandong. Repaired after review: the first disc was Weifang 80 km, which reached past Linzi, Qi's capital (Weifang-Linzi 71 km), although the page says Lai 'is on the tip of the Shandong Peninsula bordering Qi'; it is now 45 km round 118.95 E 36.75 N, which holds Changle (12 km from its centre) and reaches Linqu (45 km, at the edge), the capitals, and whose edge ends about 13 km short of Linzi (centre 57.5 km away).

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Lai (state), List of Zhou dynasty states. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -1046 is a bridge (confidence 1): the page is silent on a founding and dates no event before 567. REGION: the page names the 'tip of the Shandong Peninsula' and three capitals that lie in different places (Changle and Linqu near Weifang, Ni to the east), and the list page puts the site at the south-east of Longkou: the three-disc union is the researcher's reading, much wider than a county, because Qi 'more than doubled' on annexing it. Longkou is not a gazetteer place (coordinates used). REPAIR (2026-10-19, after the adversarial review): the first disc was Weifang 80 km, which reached Linzi, Qi's capital, and Qi's own founding disc; it is now {lon 118.95, lat 36.75, km 45} (the reviewer's figure), which holds Changle, reaches Linqu at its edge (45 km) and stops about 13 km short of Linzi (centre 57.5 km away). The Lai page (reopened) gives only 'tip of the Shandong Peninsula bordering Qi', the capitals and 'a large state'; it does not draw the frontier with Qi, so the western edge is still a reading. Residual overlaps: six cells (about 1,500 km2) of the 45 km disc fall inside the qi dossier's Zibo 60 km founding disc (the frontier strip, 118.45-118.72 E), and the whole of the ji-shandong disc (Ji, 1046-691, 118.8 E 36.76 N, 30 km) lies inside this region and holds the Changle capital dot; neither page fixes the Ji-Lai frontier, so both overlaps are left for the renderer (the smaller, earlier-ended state draws on top) and are listed in the batch notes. FOUNDING: the List of Zhou dynasty states row (reopened) reads '?-567 BCE', so 1046 stays a confidence-1 bridge. SLUG lai is Lai 萊 (annexed by Qi 567); Lai 賴 (Chu 538, ea-01-a's suggested slug 'lai') needs 'lai-2'. The qi dossier (ea-01-b) lacks the 567 gain. AREA: none on the page. Only one ruler is named (Furou, Duke Gong, ?-567), so no ruler strip.
